title: Headroom of text instructions over the task card: per-item information can fix most SearchQA failures, but what a generic rule can reach is about 0-3 points, at or below what a 200-item panel can detect
verdict_cn: 一句话：在SearchQA（检索问答）上，现有的人写任务说明已接近“任何通用文字”能达到的上限；学到的规则在它之上最多还能多0到3个百分点，比200道题能可靠分辨的差别（约3到5个百分点）还小，所以这里只能证明“不变差”，证明不了“更好”。做法：先用上一版实验和校准实验的全部现成记录统计（不花钱）；再挑60道任务说明答错的训练题做小试验，共用约129万token（模型计费单位）：让辅助模型GLM看着标准答案写“不含答案”的逐题提示，再让答题模型deepseek带着提示重答。结果：带提示后答对率从25%升到94%，但只给提示、不给题目时它也能猜中89%，等于变相给了答案；只告诉“答案恰好几个词”这一个数字，就能救回约一半错题（折合全部200题约多11个百分点）。可见剩下的错大多是答案写长或写短的逐题习惯，规则很难从题面推出：11种现成文字逐题挑最好的只多2.75个百分点，上一版学到的规则只多0到1.5个百分点。另外，各任务约一半用来检验规则的题在所有文字下都答不对；数学选择题LiveMath里“可证明更强结论”这个选项只要出现就一定是正确答案（训练题129道全是），这是数据漏洞而非能力。建议：SearchQA只做“不变差”检查；先用这些便宜的探针量出余量，再决定在哪个任务上投入。
evidence:
Labels: MEASURED = computed from data; ESTIMATED = derived under a stated assumption; CLAIM = interpretation. "TC" = task card (I-ds step-0 Skill, the five task-card seeds).

A. TC failure mass on each stage's training items over ALL TC runs (v3 plus cal-1) [MEASURED; d9_analysis3.log, section F]. Columns: items | TC pass | failure mass in item-equivalents | dead | flaky | other-text | ceiling if every non-dead item were fixed.
- SearchQA: 200 | 77.8% | 44.49 | 18.0 (40%) | 13.5 (30%) | 13.0 (29%) | +13.2 pts.
- OfficeQA: 74 | 29.1% | 52.5 | 26.0 (50%) | 18.5 (35%) | 8.0 (15%) | +35.8 pts.
- LiveMath: 100 | 34.3% | 65.7 | 34.0 (52%) | 17.7 (27%) | 14.0 (21%) | +31.7 pts.
- SpreadsheetBench: 91 | 54.0% | 41.9 | 16.0 (38%) | 16.9 (40%) | 9.0 (21%) | +28.4 pts.
- ALFWorld: 57 | 50.3% | 28.3 | 22.0 (78%) | 4.3 (15%) | 2.0 (7%) | +11.1 pts.
Median runs observed per failed item (TC / other texts / distinct other texts): SearchQA 8/82/15, OfficeQA 10/19/9, LiveMath 4/10/4, SpreadsheetBench 5/6/4, ALFWorld 3/3/2. The dead and flaky labels depend on how many runs were observed.
Failed-ITEM shares (dead / flaky / other-text): SearchQA 18/23/13 of 54; OfficeQA 26/25/8 of 59; LiveMath 34/27/14 of 75; SpreadsheetBench 15/19/9 of 43; ALFWorld 22/8/2 of 32.

B. Knowledge failures as asked: registered trigger items on which all six arms (rule, parent, 4 placebos) fail every run, screen rounds [MEASURED; reproduces the main session's figure exactly]:
- SearchQA 30/56 (53.6%)
- OfficeQA 13/26 (50.0%)
- LiveMath 7/17 (41.2%)
- SpreadsheetBench 12/30 (40.0%)
- ALFWorld 10/14 (71.4%)
- All 72/143 (50.3%); confirm rounds 10/21 (47.6%).
- Rule-vs-parent discordant items: 41/143 (28.7%).
CAVEAT [MEASURED in the pilot]: on SearchQA "dead" does NOT mean the solver cannot know the answer. Of 23 pilot items that all 11 cal-1 texts failed in all 44 runs, an oracle hint fixed 85%, and a bare "the answer has N words" hint fixed 30%.

C. Examiner codes of TC training failures (failed runs), each with dead/flaky/other-text counts [MEASURED]:
- SearchQA (90 runs):
  - FORM: D1 extra words 35 (39%; 7/16/12) and D2 other form 28 (31%; 15/5/8).
  - CONTENT: D4 wrong candidate 12 (6/2/4) and D5 wrong kind 9 (4/3/2).
  - other or noncompletion: 6.
  - Scorer view: 46/90 failed answers contain or are contained in the reference; 24 have no word overlap.
  - On the 60 pilot items (450 failed TC runs): 51.1% are a sub- or superstring of the reference (too long or too short), 31.6% share no word with it, 15.1% partially overlap.
  - References with parentheses: only 4 of 200 items.
- OfficeQA (111 runs): D2 wrong method 41 (15/18/8), D1 wrong data 30 (15/11/4), D3 calculation slip 20 (7/9/4), D5 not in document 10 (all dead), D4 answer form 5, other 5.
- LiveMath (134 runs): D1 missed the meta option 85 (63%; 58/14/13), D4 23 (1/13/9), D3 17 (6/7/4), rubric/other 6.
- SpreadsheetBench (43 runs): D4 wrong logic 25 (11/8/6); program/format codes (D1, D2, D5, D6, malformed, noncompletion) 16 (4 dead / 11 flaky / 1); D3 2.
- ALFWorld (56 runs): D3 search loop 45 (33/8/4), D1 6 (all dead), D4 5 (all dead).

D. SearchQA with cal-1 (200 items × 11 texts × 4 runs) [MEASURED]:
- Totals out of 200: ids-full (the TC) 154.5; seed-only 153.5; placebo control:2 143.0; parent:B 137.25; seed-rule 136.5; control:4 136.25; parent:A 135.75; cand 130.5; seed-rule3 129.75; control:1 128.75; control:3 116.25. No text beats the TC. Placebos alone move the scaffold by −9.8 to +3.6 points.
- 25 of 200 items fail under every text on every run. The TC fails all 4 runs on 36 items, 25 of which are dead under every text.
- Cross-fitted per-item best of 11 texts (select on 2 runs, evaluate on the other 2): +5.5 items [+1.3, +11.0], i.e. +2.75 pts [+0.6, +5.5]. The same procedure on two identical texts gives −1.75 [−4.75, +1.25].
- In-sample per-item maximum (optimistic): +12.75 items.

E. Learned v3 rules on their full focal panels, rule minus parent, item bootstrap [MEASURED; panels include each rule's own evidence items, so this is optimistic]:
- On the TC: SearchQA +0.000 [−0.036, +0.036], +0.004 [−0.019, +0.026], +0.015 [−0.011, +0.044]; LiveMath −0.022; SpreadsheetBench −0.044 (screen) and +0.027 (confirm); ALFWorld −0.140 [−0.254, −0.035].
- On the scaffold: SearchQA s1-r2 +0.055 [+0.018, +0.094] (the only interval above 0); all others between −0.013 and +0.048, intervals including 0.

F. Minimum detectable effect (80% power, two-sided 5%) = 2.8 × SD / √n [MEASURED SDs, ESTIMATED MDE]:
- Identical texts, 4 runs (SD 0.144): 2.8 pts at n = 200, 5.2 at n = 60, 12.1 at n = 11.
- Different texts, 4 runs (SD ≈ 0.22): 4.5 / 8.2 / 19.0 pts at the same sizes.
- Identical texts, 2 runs (SD 0.24): 4.8 pts at n = 200.

G. LiveMath [MEASURED on the training pool]:
- The meta option ("One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.") appears in 129 of 283 items and is the reference answer in all 129.
- On the 100 stage items: present in 45, always correct. The TC picks it in 4 of 200 runs and passes 4/90 runs on those items, versus 62/110 runs on the rest.
- ESTIMATED: a rule "pick it whenever present" would score about 76% versus the TC's 33%. This exploits how the labels were constructed; whether the test split shares this property was not examined (forbidden). D7 owns the policy call.

H. Format drift [MEASURED]: the scaffold's rate of replies with no answer tag (truncations included) rose from 0.8% (v3 training, 10-20 00:07) to 6.0% and 4.4% (screen and confirm) and to 8.2-9.5% in cal-1 that afternoon; the TC stayed at 0-0.8%. On the same 200 items the TC-minus-scaffold gap was +3.25 pts in v3 training (310 vs 297 of 400) and +9.4 pts in cal-1. CLAIM: part of cal-1's positive-control effect is the TC's robustness to this drift.

I. Prior project evidence (GLM solver, empty-Skill parent; docs/results-and-lessons.md): generic instruction minus empty +7.5 / +9.2 pts; learned minus generic +4.6 [+0.5, +9.0] and +2.9 [−1.2, +7.3]; one learning step on top of the generic instruction +2.9 [−1.1, +7.2] (p = 0.21). OfficeQA: Skills learned on other benchmarks minus the OfficeQA instruction −5.4 to −1.4 (all intervals include 0).

J. Pilot readout: see the pilot field.
design:
PILOT DESIGN (as run)
- Population: the 60 items, out of the 200 v3 stage-1 SearchQA training items, that the TC failed at least once among the v3 runs (selection used v3 runs only). These 60 hold 44.75 of the TC's 45.5 failure item-equivalents.
- Baselines:
  - cal-1 ids-full, the identical TC text, 4 runs, independent of the selection: 0.254.
  - A fresh TC run in the pilot (1 run): 0.250. Paired difference +0.005 [−0.050, +0.055]; no drift.
- Hint writer: GLM-5.3 (thinking low, temperature 0) saw the clue, the snippets, the reference answers and the TC's wrong answers. It returned {path ≤ 300 characters: which part of the clue and which snippet decide, which tempting candidate is wrong; form ≤ 150 characters: kind of answer, number of words, what to include or leave out}.
- Leak check: no reference string or reference word (unless already in the clue), and no 5-character stem. One re-ask with the violation listed, then one repair pass with length or leak feedback. Result: 55/60 valid. Of the 5 rejected, 4 stayed over length and 1 got HTTP 400 from GLM.
- Arms (deepseek-v4-flash through the frozen backends.solve and score path; temperature 0, thinking disabled; the hint rendered as a rule bullet with Skill.text_with(Rule(..., "searchqa"))):
  - tc: the TC alone, 1 run;
  - oracle: TC + "For this task: path. Answer form: form", 2 runs;
  - form: TC + the form part only, 1 run;
  - lenform: TC + the mechanical "the expected answer is exactly N word(s) long", no content, all 60 items, 1 run;
  - leak: the oracle hint ALONE, with no clue, snippets or Skill;
  - formleak: the form hint alone.
- Deviation: max_tokens 4,096 instead of 32,768. No v3 SearchQA cell had between 1,232 and 32,768 completion tokens, and no pilot cell hit the cap (all finish = stop).
- Write-once cells, hard token cap with reservation, concurrency 6.

PROPOSED v5 STANDING "HEADROOM PROBE" (run once per benchmark before any rule learning, pre-registered):
- (a) Cross-fitted per-item best of the existing k texts against the TC: free if cal-1-like data exist, otherwise k texts × 4 runs.
- (b) A mechanical form oracle: answer length for QA; analogous structural facts elsewhere (e.g. which option class, which cell range).
- (c) An oracle hint plus a hint-alone leak probe, as an upper bound only.
- Decision rule: host a "rule beats the instruction" claim only on a benchmark where (a) exceeds the MDE of the planned panel. Otherwise register the benchmark as a non-inferiority or regression stage.
- Use (b) to decide whether per-item form conventions exist that a retrieval mechanism (D2 case memory) might capture.
- Next cheap test: a "predictability probe": GLM predicts the reference word count from the clue and snippets without the reference, and that prediction is fed back as the hint. It shows how much of the +11.4 pts a reference-free mechanism could reach (about 0.3M tokens).

pilot.result:
MEASURED, 60 SearchQA training items the task card (TC) fails; 55 have a valid hint. Pass rates (item means, 95% bootstrap CI):
- cal-1 TC baseline (independent, 4 runs): 0.254 [0.163, 0.346]
- fresh TC (1 run): 0.250
- TC + oracle hint (2 runs): 0.936 [0.864, 0.991]
- TC + form-only hint (1 run): 0.909
- TC + mechanical length hint (1 run, all 60 items): 0.633 [0.517, 0.750]
- oracle hint alone, no clue or snippets: 0.891 (49/55 hints reveal the answer by themselves)
- form hint alone: 0.273 (15/55)

Paired against the cal-1 baseline (55 items):
- oracle +0.668 [+0.559, +0.777], 45 up / 0 down
- form +0.641
- length +0.386 [+0.264, +0.509], 29 up / 1 down
- oracle minus form +0.027 [−0.045, +0.109]: the reasoning path adds little beyond the form description

Recovered share of the TC failure mass:
- oracle 91.3% [82.3, 98.7] (82.1% conservatively over all 60, counting unhinted items as unrecovered)
- form 87.6% [76.6, 97.4]; 83.1% [69.0, 96.2] on the 40 items whose form hint alone does not give the answer
- length 52.8% [37.7, 68.6]
- leak-adjusted oracle on the 6 items whose full hint alone fails: 0.167 to 0.833 (n too small)

On the 200-item panel, with each hint applied only to its own failing item: oracle +36.75 items (+18.4 pts, 77.2% to 95.6%); length hint +22.75 items (+11.4 pts).

Strata:
- items dead under all 11 cal-1 texts (n=23): 0.00 to oracle 0.85, length 0.30
- D1 extra-words items (n=20): 0.23 to length 0.90
- D2 other-form items (n=16): 0.12 to length 0.44, form 0.88
- content failures D4/D5: length 0.40 / 0.60

True capability failures (the oracle fails both runs): 3/55 items, two of them still form errors ('Theatre' for 'Theater', 'state's evidence' for 'turning state's evidence').

Tokens: deepseek 1,127,286 over 395 cells (about 3.9k per TC-sized cell; 146 HTTP 429 retries; 0 unknown verdicts), GLM 164,777 over 109 calls, probe 38.

READING: the per-item oracle bound is near the trivial tell-the-answer bound (+22.75 pts) because the hints leak. The informative figure is that one integer of item-specific form information yields +11.4 pts, while the best generic text yields at most about +2.75 pts.

risks:
- The oracle hints are answer-revealing (49/55 work on their own), so the +18.4-pt oracle figure says the failures are recoverable with item-specific information; it does not bound what a rule can do. The leak-adjusted subset has only 6 items.
- GLM's form hints often carry answer-type content ("the name of a U.S. state"; 15/55 reveal the answer alone), so form versus path is not a clean split. The mechanical length hint is the clean content-free arm, but it is still item-specific and was run once.
- One benchmark only (SearchQA). The OfficeQA, LiveMath, SpreadsheetBench and ALFWorld ceilings come from observational v3 data with 2-10 TC runs per item. With so few runs the "dead" and "other-text" labels are noisy, and other-text mass may include chance passes. These ceilings are optimistic upper bounds.
- Population and baseline: the 60 items were selected on v3 runs and the baseline comes from independent cal-1 runs; the fresh run agrees (0.250 vs 0.254). These training items were reused across v3 and cal-1 (adaptive reuse). That is fine for estimating headroom but not for method claims.
- 5/60 items lack a hint and are handled in the conservative figure. max_tokens was 4,096 instead of 32,768, with no truncations observed.
- The learned-rule effects are measured on panels that contain the rules' own evidence items, so they are biased upward. That strengthens the "small" conclusion.
- The LiveMath meta-option base rate was checked only on the training pool. Its test-split rate is unknown and was not looked at by rule.
- The scaffold format drift is measured; attributing part of cal-1's +9.4 to it is an interpretation (CLAIM).
- The deepseek route is rate-limited (429s). Other explorers share it, so pilot timing varies.
recommendation:
WHAT THE OWNER SHOULD CONCLUDE ABOUT ATTAINABLE EFFECT SIZE
1. On SearchQA with deepseek and the task card, the realistic gain a learned generic rule can add is about 0 to 3 points:
- the best of the 11 existing texts chosen per item adds +2.75 [+0.6, +5.5] pts, and even that requires knowing per item which text to use;
- the v3 rules added +0.0, +0.4 and +1.5 pts;
- the earlier GLM line added +2.9 n.s.
The minimum detectable effect is 2.8-4.5 pts at 200 items × 4 runs and about 12-19 pts on an 11-item trigger set. So SearchQA cannot show "rule beats a good instruction". Register it as a non-inferiority or regression stage.
2. The headroom that does exist on SearchQA is item-specific answer-form convention, not missing knowledge. Telling the solver only the reference's word count recovers 53% of failures (+11.4 pts on the panel). A full per-item oracle recovers 91%, but those hints leak the answer. A rule can capture this only to the extent the convention is predictable from the clue; the evidence (cal-1 form-sentence arms 0 to −3 pts, best-of-11 +2.75) says the predictable part is small. Run the 0.35M-token predictability probe before any further SearchQA form-rule work.
3. About half of the gate's trigger items are dead under every arm (72/143), so effective panels are about half nominal. Remove them (D4), but do not call them knowledge failures: 85% of SearchQA items dead under all texts are fixable with item-specific information.
4. Larger nominal headroom elsewhere is mostly noise or knowledge: flaky 27-40% and dead 38-78% of the failure mass. Only 15-21% of OfficeQA, LiveMath and SpreadsheetBench failure mass shows "some other text did better", an optimistic ceiling of about 10 pts each. The one large single-sentence effect in the project, LiveMath's meta option (about +43 pts estimated on training items), is a label-construction artifact. Every LiveMath effect should be reported split into meta-option and other items, pending the owner's D7 decision.

FOR v5 AND THE PAPER
- Adopt the pre-registered headroom probe (design field) and choose the benchmark that hosts the "learned beats instruction" claim by its cross-fitted best-text gain exceeding the MDE.
- Prefer interventions that deliver per-item information at solve time (D2 case memory) if the predictability probe shows conventions cluster.
- Always compare against the task card, not the scaffold: the scaffold's format compliance drifted within one day (feed this to D5, D8 and D11).
- In the paper, present the headroom ladder (tell-the-answer +22.75; oracle hint +18.4; length +11.4; per-item best text +2.75; learned rules 0-1.5; MDE about 3-5). It turns the v3 null into a measured ceiling effect.
